rows.why: Item 11 asks which day counts as Monday and in which time zone that is judged. The run returns true for Asia/Singapore at 2026-11-22T20:00Z, which is Monday 04:00 in Singapore, and false for UTC at the same instant. So Monday is judged in the organisation's zone, as S1 expects.

Daylight saving is a case of the same question: which local day it is in the given zone. The pick formats the instant as a weekday name in the zone itself, so the zone's rules, including DST shifts, decide the local day. That is what S2 expects.

S3 makes a task with no submissions report furthest gate 0. Item 7 asks exactly that, and the run returns 0. Items 8 (max gate) and 1 (merged excluded) touch other parts of S3, but neither is settled as directly as item 7.
Item 6 asks how age in days is computed and rounded. The run gives age 1 for a task posted 1 day 23 hours earlier, so it counts whole days rounded down. That matches 9 days 23 hours giving age 9.

Item 3 asks whether exactly 14 days counts as stalled. The pick uses >= on milliseconds, and the run returns true at exactly 14 days, matching '14 days or more'. Items 4 and 5 (clock from posting, clock from latest submission) also agree with S5, but the 14-day boundary is the main thing S5 settles.
The run puts stalled task a first, then d (oldest of the rest), then b before c (same posting time, ordered by id). That is stalled first, then oldest, then id, as S6 expects.
Item 10 asks how the subject handles plurals. The run returns '1 open tasks', but S7 expects '1 open task'.
Item 2 asks what comes back when nothing is open. The run returns null, meaning no digest at all rather than an empty one, which is what S8 expects.

Item 12 asks whether the time zone is validated even when the result doesn't depend on it. S9 says Mars/Olympus fails with no conditions attached. The run throws 'Unknown time zone: Mars/Olympus' even with no tasks, and that error names the zone.
